items.claim: Clear data-focused when a focused control is disabled or unmounted. A focused Field.Control becomes disabled or unmounts. No blur event fires on that path.
items.consequence: FieldRoot keeps focused set, so data-focused stays on the root and the control, although the change description promises it no longer latches in this case.
items.proposed_fix: In `packages/react/src/field/control/FieldControl.tsx`, reset focus from the control when it becomes disabled or unmounts while focused, so `setFocused(false)` runs on that path as it does in `onBlur`.

items.claim: Should Field.Root validate receive the raw controlled value on submit?
items.consequence: If the type change is unintended and unannounced, it is a released-compatibility break and becomes a must-fix finding. If it is intended and documented, it is not a defect.
items.proposed_fix: The Base UI maintainers or the release owner: state whether the `validate` argument type for non-string controlled values is meant to change in this release, and whether it is documented.

items.claim: The description names a `processedValueRef` guard that is absent at head; the prop echo still validates once because the controlled `onChange` returns before validation.
items.consequence: `packages/react/src/field/control/FieldControl.tsx:144-145`; focused test `validates once when a controlled value is changed by the user` passes.

items.claim: The open-question paragraph says this change does not clear errors on programmatic changes, but the head's `useValueChanged` callback calls `clearErrors(name)`.

The `details.cancel()` fix takes effect only for uncontrolled inputs, so a controlled input whose consumer cancels and still sets the value runs the internal handling on the echo, which is the safer reading applied here and is not covered by any test.
items.consequence: `packages/react/src/field/control/FieldControl.tsx:144-153`; the cancel test at `FieldControl.test.tsx` is uncontrolled.
